originalFailure.scope: Public annotation proves the extra approval, but does not reveal its request identity. The subsequent controlled reproduction establishes the concrete vulnerability; it does not pretend to recover unavailable remote logs.

controlledReproduction.mechanism: Actual sandboxed Chromium: filling saves a draft callback; the fixture releases that old callback during the clicked DOM event, while intended POST approval is held. This avoids a wall-clock race. Both GET /later?draft=private-draft and POST /submit reached the approval callback; GET containing the controlled draft reached the fixture server.

redirectReproduction.mechanism: Independent actual product-adapter test granted only source origin. A 302 reached an ungranted target once before the old post-navigation check reported failure. Playwright route.continue does not re-route every redirect URL.

cause: An action-labelled click window treated all contemporaneous page requests as candidates for authorization, including background fetch/beacons unrelated to the intended navigation. Request-stage routing alone also allowed redirect targets to be contacted before the post-navigation grant check.
fix: Only a main-frame navigation armed immediately before locator.click can request consent; its single transaction slot is reserved before awaiting native consent. A rejected consent does not free that slot.
Background fetch/XHR/beacons and child-frame requests fail closed; blocked counts and notice are returned, unsupported interaction limits are visible, and a negative click result is audited BLOCKED.

A Chromium CDP response-stage guard rejects redirects before Chromium follows Location. No Node forwarding or route.fetch is introduced, so browser DNS pinning, cookies and TLS transport remain in place.
Response-guard setup failure closes the owned browser; asynchronous guard failure checks the captured browser identity before stopping it, so stale events cannot stop a later session.

The original five integration scenario assertion bodies are retained or strengthened for STOP/new-task isolation. Seven added real-browser cases cover the draft callback, main/image/iframe boundaries, blocked SPA result, owner refusal and uncertain approved POST after a blocked redirect.
A stale Playwright request callback checks the captured browser identity before reading request/frame/current state, so it cannot affect the next task after STOP.

Explicit owner refusal returns APPROVAL_DENIED and BLOCKED audit, including browsers that throw after route abort. An approved request followed by failed/blocked response returns BROWSER_EFFECT_UNCONFIRMED with a warning against retry before independent verification. Negative outcomes include error text that survives the renderer tool bridge.

verification.command: CI=true npx vitest run tests/browserSession.test.ts tests/browserPrerequisite.test.ts

independentOracles.draft: Exactly POST /submit is offered for approval; no draft GET reaches the fixture; approved POST executes once.
independentOracles.redirects: Unapproved target HTTP server receives zero requests for main navigation, image subresource and rejected iframe cases.
independentOracles.blockedSPA: No approval callback or fixture request; result ok=false, actionDispatched=true, externalEffectConfirmed=false, positive blocked count and notice; final audit BLOCKED.
independentOracles.existingSTOP: Real STOP pending approval followed by a fresh browser session succeeds. Late approval cannot send the old POST. A synthetic queued old route callback never reads request data and cannot mutate the new session audit; the new page still reads correctly. Pending-startup and stale-DNS tests remain passing.
independentOracles.ownerDenial: One explicit native refusal; no POST sent; APPROVAL_DENIED result and BLOCKED final audit.
independentOracles.approvedPOSTRedirect: Approved POST actually reaches fixture once. Its redirect target receives zero requests. Result remains uncertain with BROWSER_EFFECT_UNCONFIRMED and explicit no-retry-without-verification text; final audit UNCONFIRMED, never rollback claimed.

limits: Supported interaction is a single owner-approved main-frame navigation; SPA background submits, child-frame forms and automatic HTTP redirects are explicitly unsupported.

The adapter does not prove that a main-frame navigation was causally triggered by the clicked element; a timer navigation during the armed interval remains possible. The exact actual URL, method and body require owner approval, and only one transaction may claim the click.

Response-stage guard checks were exercised with real Chromium. Independent reviewer also checked a dedicated-worker redirect under the same guard; this is not a claim covering every possible worker/browser topology.
These are controlled adapter tests, not real-model chat or target-desktop acceptance. Remote CI rerun after this patch remains pending parent commit/push.

ownerDenialReproduction.mechanism: Independent reviewer observed native approval=false, actual POST count0, but old result ok=true and click COMPLETED. The new exact outcome regression now requires APPROVAL_DENIED, error text, zero POSTs and BLOCKED audit.

logNormalization: Trailing whitespace/empty EOF lines only; all diagnostic text retained
